classes.rule: Full CI runs exactly once per commit that matters, inside the Actions minutes the account includes: on pull_request (opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review) for non-draft pull requests, and on push to the declared branches (kit.canon.json workflows.ci.branches, main by default), never on a push to every branch or to a wildcard, so a pull request commit is never tested twice (push and pull_request) and an agent's branch push is gated by the local pre-push hook, not by a runner; every job of a workflow that runs on pull_request skips a draft; a schedule is at most weekly unless a reviewed exception in workflows.ci.schedule_exceptions names the cron and the reason; and a workflow_run observer allocates no runner unless its condition on the triggering run's conclusion holds (a job-level if). A workflow that runs on pull_request carries no path filter (`paths` or `paths-ignore`): a required check that a path filter skips stays pending, so an ordinary pull request that changes only release.json or a wrangler config could never merge. The pull request that automation opens for the resilience records (a GITHUB_TOKEN pull request, authored by github-actions[bot]) needs no filter: GitHub holds its pull_request run as action_required, which creates no job check and conflicts with nothing, and the required check on its head comes from the push run of the records branch. The check on its head commit comes from a push run (a workflow_dispatch run does not satisfy a ruleset's required status check): the workflow named records.workflow lists the records branch pattern `<records.branch_prefix>**` in on.push.branches and has a job named exactly records.check (default `test (ubuntu-24.04)`), and the records step pushes with the repository's write deploy key, because a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflow; a step that opens a pull request (`gh pr create`) takes the records branch and files from `kit release records`, writes none of them itself, and dispatches nothing. A push trigger lists the declared branches and the records branch pattern, nothing else. The class reads the workflows of templates/ci as well as .github/workflows.

detect.problem: a push trigger that is not bounded to the declared branches: `push:` with no `branches`, `branches: ['**']`, `claude/**` or any wildcard, `branches-ignore`, or `on: push`, runs the whole suite for every agent push to every branch and, with pull_request, tests every pull request commit twice. Run full CI on pull_request (non-draft) and `push: branches: [main]` (kit.canon.json workflows.ci.branches); the local pre-push hook is the gate for a branch push A push that lists both branches and tags runs a release tag's commit a second time (it was tested on main): put tags in a workflow of their own.; the one other branch pattern a push may list is the records branch pattern `<kit.canon.json workflows.ci.records.branch_prefix>**` (default `resilience-records/**`): the push of the records branch is what produces the required check on the records pull request's head commit

a pull_request trigger without the declared types, or a pull_request_target one (it runs the base branch's workflow for every pull request commit and is no draft-guarded, once-per-commit run): `pull_request:` alone runs on opened, synchronize and reopened but never on ready_for_review, so a draft marked ready would sit with no run. Declare `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]`, exactly those four

a job of a workflow that runs on pull_request that does not skip a draft pull request: a draft runs no full CI (an agent marks it ready when done, which triggers the run). Put `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.draft == false` on the job (or `(that) && <more>`; a job that never runs on a pull request says `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`, or lists the events it runs on: `github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`)

a schedule that runs more often than weekly, or more than one cron that is not a declared exception (each fires on its own: two weekly crons are twice a week): every cron fire allocates a runner, and a minutes budget does not survive `*/N` or a daily job nobody reads. Use one fixed minute and hour on one weekday (`17 3 * * 1`) or one day of the month, or declare the cron with its reason in kit.canon.json workflows.ci.schedule_exceptions ([{ cron, reason }], reviewed)

a workflow_run observer job with no condition on the triggering run's conclusion: without a job-level `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == '<outcome>'` every completed run of the observed workflow allocates a runner to do nothing. Put the condition on the job (alone, or `&&` more; never `||`, which lets the observer run anyway), so a skipped job allocates no runner and costs no minutes

a workflow the records pull request would start, or the one that stands in for it, off the records constants of kit.canon.json workflows.ci.records: a path filter (`paths` or `paths-ignore`) on its pull_request trigger. A required check that a path filter skips stays pending, so an ordinary pull request that changes only release.json or a wrangler config could never merge: remove the filter. The records pull request (github-actions[bot], GITHUB_TOKEN) needs none: GitHub holds its pull_request run as action_required, which creates no job check, and its required check comes from the PUSH run of the records branch. The required check on the records head commit comes from a PUSH run: the workflow named `records.workflow` (default test) lists `<records.branch_prefix>**` in `on.push.branches` and has a job whose `name` is exactly `records.check` (default `test (ubuntu-24.04)`). A workflow_dispatch run does not satisfy a ruleset's required status check, and a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflow, so the records step pushes with the repository's write deploy key (RECORDS_DEPLOY_KEY)

a step that opens a pull request (`gh pr create`) that does not take its constants from kit.canon.json workflows.ci.records, or that dispatches a workflow: the branch (`kit release records branch`) and the files it commits (`kit release records paths`) are each written once and asked for, never written again in a workflow (a step that names the branch prefix, release.json or a wrangler config or any other path of workflows.ci.records.paths itself holds a second list that drifts from `kit release records paths`); and it never runs `gh workflow run`: a workflow_dispatch run does not satisfy a ruleset's required status check, so the records pull request would never merge. The check comes from the push of the records branch, made with the repository's write deploy key

classes.rule: Code that runs git names the environment git runs in, and that environment is gitEnv() (packages/cli/src/git.js; forge, which has no dependencies, its own gitEnv), or gitEnv(env, { keep: ["GIT_INDEX_FILE"] }) when the call must run against another index (the commit in progress): the one declared keep form, a literal array of exactly that one name, which drops git's own repository-local variables (git rev-parse --local-env-vars). Git exports GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE and the rest to every hook, so a git call in the caller's environment (none named, process.env, a spread of it, an unchecked variable) reads the hook's repository, not the directory it was given (-C, cwd). Only the call's own options object counts (not an env inside another argument or a nested call), and only env: gitEnv() or env: { PATH: process.env.PATH }. Any call whose first argument names git counts, whatever the function is called (an alias, a wrapper, execSync's command string, a path to git).

classes.rule: Every job of every GitHub Actions workflow runs on the one runner image kit.canon.json declares (workflows.runner), or on workflows.canary.runner in a job with continue-on-error, never on a *-latest label GitHub re-points on its own schedule; ${{ matrix.runner }} is followed into the matrix values, and a runs-on that cannot be read, a runner that is not declared, or a repository that declares no runner is refused (fail closed).
first_seen: kit#59@a7b44d8 (2026-10-01): GitHub moves ubuntu-latest to Ubuntu 26 between 2026-10-19 and 2026-11-19, and a floating label would move every repository's CI with it; the hand-written check this class replaces (wo-0016) was written for it

detect.problem: a workflow without jobs, or a job (not a reusable-workflow call) without a readable runs-on: a runner that cannot be read cannot be pinned, so the gate refuses it; declare runs-on on every job

a job whose runs-on is a label that is not the one runner image kit.canon.json declares (workflows.runner, or workflows.canary.runner on a job that may fail): a floating *-latest label that GitHub re-points on its own schedule, another image, a list of several labels; use the declared image

a job whose runs-on is a runner group or labels object ({ group, labels }): it runs on whatever the group or the labels hold on the day, so the image is not pinned and the gate cannot read it; use the declared image (workflows.runner of kit.canon.json), or ${{ matrix.runner }}

a job whose runs-on is an expression other than ${{ matrix.runner }} written exactly so (${{ matrix.os }}, ${{ inputs.runner }}, ${{ vars.RUNNER }}, ${{matrix.runner}}, ...): the gate follows only matrix.runner into strategy.matrix, and an expression it cannot follow is a runner it cannot pin; name the declared image, or use ${{ matrix.runner }} with the images in strategy.matrix

a job that runs on ${{ matrix.runner }} whose matrix gives the runner no value, or a value that is not the declared image (strategy.matrix.include[*].runner or strategy.matrix.runner[*] must each be workflows.runner or workflows.canary.runner of kit.canon.json)

a job that runs the canary image (workflows.canary.runner) in a shape other than the declared one: a job that runs only the canary has continue-on-error: true (the boolean); a canary leg of a matrix is an include leg { runner: <canary image>, canary: true } beside legs with canary: false, with continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.canary }} written exactly so. ${{ false }}, "true", ${{ true }}, any other expression, or a canary in a runner list leaves the canary able to block, or the pinned image unable to

kit.canon.json declares a floating *-latest label as the CI runner (workflows.runner or workflows.canary.runner): GitHub re-points it on its own schedule; declare an explicit versioned image such as ubuntu-24.04

classes.rule: Every uses: of a workflow job or step names a ref that is not a branch, in any case and not in the refs/heads/ or refs/tags/ form (a release tag or a commit sha; the branch names are workflows.branch_refs of kit.canon.json, default main, master, HEAD, latest, dev, develop, trunk), a docker:// image names a tag other than latest or a digest, and only local ./ actions need no ref.
first_seen: kit#59@a7b44d8 (2026-10-01): an action pinned to a branch runs whatever the branch holds on the day, so CI is no longer the code that was reviewed; the hand-written check this class replaces (wo-0016) was written for it

detect.problem: a uses: that names no ref or floats on a branch (@main, @Main, @refs/heads/main, @refs/tags/v1, ...), or a docker image without a pinned tag or digest: pin a release tag or a commit sha written as the bare name (branch names are compared without regard to case, and an explicit refs/heads/ or refs/tags/ form is refused), so the workflow runs the code that was reviewed (local ./ actions are fine)

classes.rule: A repository declares its CI runner policy (kit.canon.json workflows) and has at least one workflow file in .github/workflows (workflows.required: false is the one declared exception), or has no .github/workflows at all and says so with the declared not-applicable reason notApplicable.workflows.predicate no-workflows, which the kit proves from the files: a repository with no workflows block is NOT CONFIGURED and fails (t=0), never a pass, and a not-applicable reason over a repository that has workflows is refused.
first_seen: kit#59@a7b44d8 (2026-10-01): the runner policy is declared once in kit.canon.json and a repository with no workflow has nothing it applies to; the hand-written check this class replaces (wo-0016) failed it

detect.problem: workflows: NOT CONFIGURED (docs/CONSTITUTION.md, t=0): kit.canon.json declares no CI runner policy (workflows), or declares one over a repository with no workflow in .github/workflows. Declare workflows { runner, canary } and add a workflow that runs npm ci && npm test; or, when the repository has no .github/workflows at all, declare "notApplicable": { "workflows": { "predicate": "no-workflows" } } (the kit proves from the files that there is no workflow); or declare workflows.required: false

classes.rule: The canary runner image declared in kit.canon.json (workflows.canary) is reviewed by its review_by date: past it the check fails until the canary is promoted to workflows.runner and every runs-on re-pinned, or the date is moved with a reason.
first_seen: kit#59@a7b44d8 (2026-10-01): a canary that nobody reviews becomes the permanent unpinned image; the review date forces the promotion; the hand-written check this class replaces (wo-0016) failed it

detect.problem: the CI canary image is past its review_by date (kit.canon.json workflows.canary.review_by): promote it to workflows.runner and re-pin every runs-on, or move the date with a reason

the CI canary image declares no review_by date (kit.canon.json workflows.canary.review_by): a canary with no date never expires and becomes the permanent unpinned image; declare the date it is reviewed by (YYYY-MM-DD)

classes.rule: A module decides it runs as the program by comparing realpathSync(process.argv[1]) with fileURLToPath(import.meta.url). Node loads the main module by its real path, so process.argv[1] as given (or resolve()d, or matched by file name) differs through a symlinked checkout or worktree, and the program silently does nothing, exit 0: npm test green with no test run. The accepted form compares inside a try whose catch answers not run directly, since argv[1] can name no file (node -) and a guard that throws breaks every import of the module.
first_seen: kit#122@aca80ba confirming review: packages/cli/scripts/test-run.mjs compared process.argv[1] unresolved, so npm test through a symlinked path ran nothing and exited 0; the same guard in forge upstream-sync, plugins kit-plugin-check and site templatize

kit#122@3460921 confirming review: a file:// template of argv[1], process.argv.at(1) and fs.realpathSync were not read right, and the bare realpathSync guard throws on node - (forge cli.js already used the try form)
kit#122@1a74af3 confirming review: a realpathSync in a catch or finally block, or in a try without a catch, counted as inside a try

((binary_expression left: (subscript_expression object: (member_expression) @o index: (number) @n) @finding ["===" "==" "!==" "!="]) (#eq? @o "process.argv") (#eq? @n "1"))
((binary_expression ["===" "==" "!==" "!="] right: (subscript_expression object: (member_expression) @o index: (number) @n) @finding) (#eq? @o "process.argv") (#eq? @n "1"))
((call_expression function: (_) @f arguments: (arguments (subscript_expression object: (member_expression) @o index: (number) @n) @finding)) (#eq? @o "process.argv") (#eq? @n "1") (#not-match? @f "(^|\\.)realpathSync(\\.native)?$"))
((member_expression object: (subscript_expression object: (member_expression) @o index: (number) @n) @finding) (#eq? @o "process.argv") (#eq? @n "1"))
((template_substitution (subscript_expression object: (member_expression) @o index: (number) @n) @finding) (#eq? @o "process.argv") (#eq? @n "1"))
((call_expression function: (member_expression object: (member_expression) @o property: (property_identifier) @p) arguments: (arguments (number) @n)) @finding (#eq? @o "process.argv") (#eq? @p "at") (#eq? @n "1"))
detect.problem: decides it runs as the program from process.argv[1] as given (or process.argv.at(1)): through a symlink it never matches and the program does nothing, exit 0. Compare realpathSync(process.argv[1]) with fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), inside a try whose catch answers not run directly

unless.why: in the body of a try that has a catch: a process.argv[1] that names no file (node -, an extensionless main) answers not run directly instead of throwing at import (a catch or finally block, or a try without a catch, does not)

detect.problem: resolves process.argv[1] outside a try: when argv[1] names no file (node -) realpathSync throws, and every import of the module fails. Wrap the comparison in a try whose catch answers not run directly

classes.rule: A test never makes a temporary directory itself: it does not call mkdtemp, mkdtempSync (or the Disposable forms) from node:fs, fs, fs.promises or an alias of them, a destructured name or a computed key. It takes the directory from the test helper, tempDir(t, prefix) for one test or fileTempDir(prefix) for one file, which removes it when the test or the file ends, whatever the result. The helper module, packages/core/test/support/temp.mjs, is the one file excluded from the class and the one place that calls mkdtemp.
first_seen: kit@88f87e4 findings.test.mjs made kit-findings-* directories with mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), ...)) and never removed them
2026-10-07: /tmp filled twice, thousands of kit-* directories (6.8 GB), from 110 mkdtemp calls in 41 test files run directly with node --test, outside the per-run TMPDIR of npm test

detect.problem: a test makes its own temporary directory with mkdtemp and nothing removes it: it stays in the host's temp directory for good (node --test <file> runs outside the per-run TMPDIR of npm test). Take it from the test helper (packages/core/test/support/temp.mjs): tempDir(t, prefix) in a test, fileTempDir(prefix) at the top level of a file

classes.rule: A capability registry entry (*.capability.json) carries an id of the form <code>.capability.<domain>.<action>, where <code> is a project the kit capability engine serves (the registry's capabilityEngine flag, packages/core/registry/projects.json; the pattern is generated from it by packages/core/scripts/project-codes.mjs): any other prefix is refused, because a project that builds its own native engine never shares the kit's.
first_seen: Owner correction 2026-10-07 (007dude): a project's own native engine must not share the kit engine; the first draft of wo-0017-capability-first listed a native engine's capability ids among the kit engine's id prefixes

detect.problem: a capability id outside the kit engine's projects: ids are <code>.capability.* for a project the registry marks capabilityEngine; a project with its own native engine keeps its capabilities there

classes.rule: The rendered gates never stop running silently: every browser test file (a test file that imports browser-env.mjs, however it is named; the set is declared once, in this class's files.importing, and is what npm test's browser step runs) and browser-env itself carry no skip or todo, whether written as an option ({ skip }, { "skip": x }, { ["skip"]: x }), a call (test.skip, t.skip(), t["skip"]()), a destructured name or an import. A missing browser fails them on every machine.
first_seen: kit#115 round 2 review of 36d51ec: without a browser and without CI set every theme-qa, visual-qa and search-qa test was skipped and npm test exited 0, including the npm test that deploy:web runs (2026-10-07)
kit#115 round 3 review of a2d3118: the skip scan was a regex, then a raw query that missed subscript calls, destructuring patterns and computed keys (2026-10-07)
kit#115 review of e339664 (2026-10-07): the scope was a hard-coded list of three test files and browser-env, so browser-bounds and browser-ci, which are browser files, were not covered

detect.query:
(pair key: [(property_identifier) (string)] @k (#match? @k "^.?(skip|todo).?$")) @finding
((shorthand_property_identifier) @finding (#match? @finding "^(skip|todo)$"))
((shorthand_property_identifier_pattern) @finding (#match? @finding "^(skip|todo)$"))
(pair_pattern key: [(property_identifier) (string)] @k (#match? @k "^.?(skip|todo).?$")) @finding
(pair key: (computed_property_name [(string) (template_string)] @k) (#match? @k "^.?(skip|todo).?$")) @finding
(member_expression property: (property_identifier) @k (#match? @k "^(skip|todo)$")) @finding
(subscript_expression index: [(string) (template_string)] @k (#match? @k "^.?(skip|todo).?$")) @finding
(import_specifier name: (identifier) @k (#match? @k "^(skip|todo)$")) @finding
(import_specifier alias: (identifier) @k (#match? @k "^(skip|todo)$")) @finding
detect.problem: a browser test is skipped or marked todo: the rendered gates must run everywhere and fail without a browser (packages/cli/test/browser-env.mjs); remove the skip/todo

classes.rule: A test file or test helper reaches a browser only through browser-env.mjs: one under */test/ that imports playwright, playwright-core, chromium or the bounded launcher (browser-guard) in any written form (import, re-export, import(), require, createRequire(…)("playwright"), a template literal without substitutions), or calls launchGuarded or chromium.launch, without importing browser-env.mjs (directly or through relative imports, to a fixed point) is refused, because npm test's serial browser step is the set of files that reach browser-env.mjs and a browser file outside it would run in parallel and unchecked. A test that imports a helper which reaches a browser is checked through the helper (helpers under */test/ are scanned). A static query cannot see a variable specifier (import(name)), a browser launched in a child process (spawn of a script or of the Chromium binary) or a helper outside */test/: those are outside this gate's reach, and a reviewer reads them.
first_seen: kit#115 review of e339664 (2026-10-07): browser files were classified by the text browser-env.mjs, so a test file that launched a browser some other way ran in the parallel step, where browser files crashed pages and hung (2026-10-07)
kit#115 confirming review of 39e0fff (2026-10-07): the scan looked one import deep and only at *.test.mjs, and missed import(`playwright`) and createRequire(import.meta.url)("playwright")

(export_statement source: (string (string_fragment) @finding) (#match? @finding "^(playwright|playwright-core|chromium)(/.*)?$|(^|/)browser-guard(\.js)?$"))

(call_expression function: (import) arguments: (arguments . (template_string . (string_fragment) @finding .)) (#match? @finding "^(playwright|playwright-core|chromium)(/.*)?$|(^|/)browser-guard(\.js)?$"))
(call_expression function: (identifier) @fn arguments: (arguments . (string (string_fragment) @finding)) (#eq? @fn "require") (#match? @finding "^(playwright|playwright-core|chromium)(/.*)?$|(^|/)browser-guard(\.js)?$"))
(call_expression arguments: (arguments . (string (string_fragment) @finding)) (#match? @finding "^(playwright|playwright-core)(/.*)?$"))

(call_expression function: (identifier) @finding (#eq? @finding "launchGuarded"))
(call_expression function: (member_expression property: (property_identifier) @finding) (#eq? @finding "launchGuarded"))
(call_expression function: (member_expression object: (member_expression property: (property_identifier) @obj) property: (property_identifier) @finding) (#eq? @obj "chromium") (#eq? @finding "launch"))
detect.problem: a test file or helper reaches a browser without importing browser-env.mjs: import it (loadPlaywright, CHROMIUM) so the file is a browser file that npm test runs in the serial browser step, with a floor, and no skip

classes.rule: The vendored kit snapshot's location has one source: kit.canon.json "vendor" (path, manifest), read through packages/cli/src/vendor-path.js (DEFAULT_VENDOR_PATH when none is declared, snapshotRoots, vendorRoots, repoSnapshotRoots). Kit code never names the snapshot by a literal vendor/kit path: a literal is a second source that a custom vendor.path silently escapes (the guard's generated roots, the launcher's hook lookup, the canon's no-vendored-kit predicate, the trust directories, the watcher step). A comment line is documentation, not a source. A shell file that cannot import vendor-path.js may mirror the default on exactly one line marked kit:default-vendor-path, which a test holds equal to DEFAULT_VENDOR_PATH.
first_seen: kit#139@832e86a independent review (2026-10-09): with a custom vendor.path the generated-file rule still matched only vendor/kit/**, and launcher.sh, canon/facts.js, canon/findings.js, content-state.js and resilience/check.js still named vendor/kit, so a custom path escaped the guard and waived the snapshot proof

detect.problem: a literal vendor/kit in kit code: the snapshot is wherever kit.canon.json vendor.path says. Read it through packages/cli/src/vendor-path.js (snapshotRoots, vendorRoots, repoSnapshotRoots, DEFAULT_VENDOR_PATH)

classes.rule: Only three things talk to a project's comms engine: the engine itself, the @saasreport/channels email adapter (announcements and monitor alerts) and submitForm (@saasreport/core/form-deliveries), which hands every form to POST /v1/comms/submit so the receipt and the owner's copy go together and are recorded. No other file names the COMMS binding (a property of any object or alias, optional or not, an index by string or by a constant, a destructuring name) or builds a v1/comms/ URL, and nothing outside the engine reads the owner's address secret (the set owner-secret-names, held equal to forms.owner.secret's enum), so no form handler, however it is split across files, can send the receipt alone (docs/FORMS.md). The limit: computed access is closed only where the name is visible in the same file (a string, a template, a constant declared there); env[name] with a name that is imported, passed in or concatenated is not, and a handler that does that is caught by review and by the engine's own refusal of a form's template on /v1/comms/dispatch (409 form_template_requires_submit), not by this gate.
first_seen: the form handlers of four downstream sites: receipts sent, owner alert optional and swallowed, OPS_NOTIFY_TO empty: 16 receipts and 0 owner notifications in the four ledgers, owner report 2026-10-13
SaasReport/kit packages/cloudflare/src/handlers/events.js@062456db: POST /api/forms/event-rsvp with no owner notification

review of SaasReport/kit 7cd5873 (2026-10-13): the first form of the class matched only a file that both routed /api/forms and dispatched, so a handler split across a route file and a sender file, env["COMMS"] or a built URL passed

review of SaasReport/kit 74113248 (2026-10-13): the text pattern missed env?.COMMS, env[BINDING], a multi-line destructure, aliases, a template v1/comms/${kind} URL and const { OPS_NOTIFY_TO } = env, and hardcoded the secret's name; the gate now reads the syntax tree

detect.problem: the comms engine reached outside submitForm and the channels email adapter: a form goes to POST /v1/comms/submit (submitForm), which sends the receipt and the owner's copy together and records both; an announcement or an alert goes through the channels email adapter. Read from the syntax tree, so env?.COMMS, env[NAME], { COMMS } = env over several lines, an alias (bindings.COMMS, e.COMMS) and a built v1/comms/ URL are all this reach

the owner's address read outside the comms engine: whether the owner hears of a submission is decided by the engine (forms.owner.secret, whose names are the registry set owner-secret-names), never by a site's handler

classes.rule: A repository with a comms.config.js runs `kit comms check` in its npm test script: the build gate of form coverage (a form the site posts that the comms config does not declare is refused by the engine and nobody hears of it) is a step nobody can forget, because it is part of the test that must pass before every push and deploy (docs/FORMS.md).
first_seen: review of SaasReport/kit 74113248 (2026-10-13): `kit comms check` existed as the form-coverage gate and no repository's npm test ran it

detect.problem: this repository has a comms.config.js and its npm test script does not run `kit comms check`: the form-coverage gate (every form the site posts is declared in the comms config) would never run. Add `kit comms check` to the test script

classes.rule: A repository that vendors the kit (kit.canon.json vendor) or deploys a Worker (release.json) runs the freshness verifier on a schedule: .github/workflows/staleness.yml has a schedule trigger and every job of it runs `kit check staleness`. A repository that can go stale and never asks is stale without anyone knowing (docs/FRESHNESS.md: a verifier proves it continuously).
first_seen: owner mandate 2026-10-13: staleness must be structurally impossible across the estate; four sites ran a kit 50 to 68 commits behind main, a branch 0 commits behind its origin looked current, and nothing asked the remote

detect.problem: this repository vendors the kit or deploys a Worker (release.json) and has no .github/workflows/staleness.yml: nothing asks whether it is stale. Copy templates/ci/staleness.yml from the kit (docs/FRESHNESS.md)

the freshness workflow does not run on a schedule, or a job of it does not run `kit check staleness`: a verifier that never runs proves nothing. Keep the schedule trigger and the `kit check staleness --json` step of templates/ci/staleness.yml

classes.rule: A repository holds the kit at t=0 or not at all: kit.canon.json vendor.mode is "source" (the kit is a checkout at its head, fetched and verified against the published head object before every use by the committed bootstrap scripts/kit.mjs, nothing of it committed), never a snapshot (a copy at one commit with a manifest, which goes stale and is re-vendored after the fact). Owner mandate 2026-10-27: re-vendoring is post-facto; all must be t=0.
first_seen: owner mandate 2026-10-27: a central deploy repository's main ran a vendored kit 49 commits behind and failed 32 scheduled deploys on it; a downstream site vendored a kit of 2026-10-07; a re-vendor workflow (kit#218) was refused as post-facto: the kit is resolved at its head at the moment of use, or refused

detect.problem: kit.canon.json holds the kit as a snapshot (vendor without mode "source"): a copy that goes stale and is re-vendored after the fact. Run kit source init: the kit becomes a checkout at its head, verified before every use (docs/FRESHNESS.md, the kit at t=0)

classes.rule: `kit check staleness` reads the outside world (the remote head, a Worker's /api/build, the kit's head), so its answer changes without any commit: it runs only in a workflow whose `on` is schedule and workflow_dispatch (never pull_request, push or workflow_call, which another workflow can call from a push), and never in an npm test, pretest, posttest, prepare, push or pre-push script, a git hook (.githooks, .husky), a pre-push script or a Makefile. A finding is an obligation and an alert, never a red main by itself (docs/FRESHNESS.md, the clock rule).
first_seen: review of SaasReport/kit 0a1493e1 (2026-10-13): the clock rule (a finding never turns main red) was a sentence in docs/FRESHNESS.md and nothing stopped the verifier from being put in the test that gates every push

detect.problem: a workflow runs `kit check staleness` and is triggered by pull_request, push or workflow_call (or by an `on` the gate cannot read as scheduled only): the verifier reads the live world, so its result is not a property of the commit, and a finding would turn a pull request or main red (a reusable workflow can be called from either). Run it only from a workflow whose `on` is schedule and workflow_dispatch

an npm test, push or hook script runs `kit check staleness`: the verifier reads the live world, so a finding would fail every push and every test run for a reason no commit caused. It belongs to the scheduled workflow only (docs/FRESHNESS.md)

a git hook, a pre-push script or a Makefile runs `kit check staleness`: the verifier reads the live world, so a finding would stop every push or build for a reason no commit caused. It belongs to the scheduled workflow only (docs/FRESHNESS.md)

classes.rule: A schema that gives a fact a verification day, a date-typed property (format date or the date pattern) named in registry/staleness.json verification_days (verified, checked, verifiedOn, testedOn, readOn, retrieved), says how old the day may be: the same `properties` object declares `max_age_days`, or the schema references kit.dated-registry.v1 in its allOf (top-level max_age_days). A verification day with no declared age can never be stale, so `kit check staleness` could never report it. A property of that name that is an enum of statuses, a const, a boolean or a $ref (holiday-pack and concept-catalogue `accuracy.status`) is not a day and is not covered. Local $refs ("#/$defs/...") are followed first, so a verification day behind a $ref to a $defs date is caught and one behind a $ref to an enum, const or boolean is not; a reference that cannot be followed (another file) is not judged.
first_seen: review of SaasReport/kit 0a1493e1 (2026-10-13): github-orgs.schema.json (claude/kit-deploy-secrets-plan) declares `verified` as a date pattern per org and no max age, so its facts could never go stale

detect.problem: a schema declares a verification day (a date named in registry/staleness.json verification_days: verified, checked, verifiedOn, testedOn, readOn, retrieved) and no `max_age_days` beside it, and does not reference kit.dated-registry.v1: the fact can never be reported stale. Add max_age_days to the same properties, or write the schema with allOf [{ "$ref": "dated-registry.schema.json" }]

classes.rule: Every tag of a tag vocabulary (tags.config.json, kit.content-tags.v1) names a colour role of the project's tokens (chart1 to chart6, accent, ok, warn, err) and never a literal colour or no colour: a tag painted by a value cannot be proven readable by the colour canon, and an uncoloured tag is the defect the vocabulary exists to end (docs/TAGS.md).
first_seen: a downstream app's podcasts, blog and series, owner brief 2026-10-14 ("fix all tag problems end to end for all sites"): episodes and series carried no tags at all, blog tags had no colour and no page; the class keeps the fix from being undone by a tag painted with a hex

detect.problem: a tag of the vocabulary has no colour role, or a colour that is not a role of the project's tokens (a hex, rgb() or named colour): every tag is painted by a tone role (chart1 to chart6, accent, ok, warn, err), whose derived on-role text colour the colour canon proves readable

classes.rule: A repository with podcasts, a blog or a tag vocabulary declares its `tags` block in kit.canon.json, so `kit check tags` checks every series, item and post against the vocabulary: without the block tags are free text again and nothing colours, lists or checks them (docs/TAGS.md).
first_seen: owner brief 2026-10-14 ("fix all tag problems end to end for all sites"): sites with podcasts and a blog carried untyped tags because nothing declared a vocabulary; the class refuses a site that adopts the kit without declaring its tags

detect.problem: this repository has podcasts, a blog or a tag vocabulary and kit.canon.json has no `tags` block, so no tag is ever checked against the vocabulary: add to kit.canon.json "tags": { "vocabulary": "tags.config.json" } and write tags.config.json (kit.content-tags.v1, docs/TAGS.md)

classes.rule: Every tag a podcast series, an episode item or a blog post names is a tag of the project's vocabulary (kit.canon.json tags.vocabulary), each series and post names at least one, and no list names a tag twice: a tag is defined once, so it can be coloured, listed and filtered, and a free-text tag cannot reappear (docs/TAGS.md).
first_seen: owner brief 2026-10-14 ("fix all tag problems end to end for all sites"): the same topic was spelled several ways in blog front matter and series carried no tags, because a tag was text typed beside the content and nothing checked it

detect.problem: a series, or one of its items, names a tag that is not in the tag vocabulary (or a series names none, or a list names a tag twice): a series names at least one tag from the vocabulary, its items inherit them or name their own, and a tag exists only where the vocabulary defines it (docs/TAGS.md)
a blog post names no tag, or names a tag that is not in the tag vocabulary (or names one twice): a post's front matter lists at least one tag, each defined in the vocabulary (docs/TAGS.md)

classes.rule: No workflow runs on the push of an archive branch. The naming constitution archives to a branch `archive/<date>/...` before anything is deleted; that branch is a frozen copy, not work, and a workflow that runs on its push runs the project's own jobs (tests, a daily veto, a deploy) against a copy that must not move anything. Every workflow with `on.push` therefore either lists only branch patterns that `archive/<date>/<name>` does not match (`branches`, each pattern decided by the pattern itself, in GitHub's filter syntax: a pattern with `**` is refused when the text before its first `**` can start an archive branch (the free-form name can be the literal rest), a pattern without `**` when its first segment can match `archive` and two more segments follow is tested against the whole pattern; so `**`, `*/**`, `a*/**`, `**/x`, `archive/**`, `archive/2026-10-14/**` and `archive/**/prod` are refused, and `main`, `releases/**`, `release-records/**` and `archive*` (one segment, no `/`) are not), or carries `branches-ignore` containing `archive/**`, or names only `tags`. GitHub does not allow `branches` and `branches-ignore` on one event, so a push that already lists its branches needs nothing more. `pull_request` and `pull_request_target` are not in this class: their `branches` filter matches the BASE branch of the pull request, never the head, so it cannot keep an archive push from running anything, and the push of an archive branch starts no pull_request run. A workflow triggered only by schedule, workflow_dispatch, workflow_run or workflow_call is exempt. The kit's CI templates carry it.
first_seen: a downstream repository (2026-10-13): a push to branch archive/2026-10-13/... ran veto-daily.yml, a workflow whose push trigger named no branch, against the archived copy

detect.problem: a workflow that runs on push without excluding archive branches: the push of an `archive/<date>/...` branch (the archive of the naming constitution) would run it. Give the push trigger `branches-ignore: ['archive/**']`, or list only the branches it runs on (`branches: [main]`; every pattern is decided existentially in GitHub's filter syntax, never by a list of sample branches, so `**`, `*/**`, `a*/**`, `**/x`, `**/release`, `archive/*/*`, `archive/2026-10-14/**` and `archive/**/prod` are refused); a push trigger of `tags` only is exempt, and so is a workflow with only schedule, workflow_dispatch, workflow_run, workflow_call or pull_request triggers
